title: Functional Consequences of Early Childhood Otitis Media
text:
Otitis media is the second most common reason children go to the doctor. This project will
provide evidence of long-lasting functional listening deficits in children resulting from otitis media after
the pathology has resolved. This will have a significant theoretical and translational impact on the
early identification and intervention of pediatric hearing loss resulting from otitis media.

title: Neurodevelopmental Stem Cell core
text: ABSTRACT – CORE B Synaptic GEF and GAPs have emerged as significant players in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). While a large number of clinical variants have been reported in these genes in patients with NDDs, their molecular and cellular consequences have not been systematically analyzed. The precise biological functions of synaptic GEF and GAP in human neuronal subtypes remain unclear, while there are no chemical tool compounds that can acutely manipulate their catalytic activity. Recent advances in the generation and differentiation of patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offer new opportunities for elucidating the pathogenic mechanisms of NDDs. Certain unique capabilities of iPSC technologies are well suited for the study of NDDs, including providing a platform for examining the effects of genetic approaches or chemical probes on human neuron activity, morphology, and developmental processes, and enabling investigations of distinct human neuronal subtypes. Our Center proposes to study genetic variants in human synaptic GEF and GAP genes and their associated phenotypes in human iPSC-derived neurons. The overarching goal of Core B is to provide high quality, efficient and cost-effective services to Center members related to iPSC technologies. Core B will have an exclusive focus on the neurobiology of NDDs. Core B will align with the goals of Projects 1 and 2 to interrogate NDD-relevant cellular and network phenotypes. All data and cell lines generated by the Neurodevelopmental Stem Cell Core will be shared with the members of our Center and the broader academic community. The specific aims of the Neurobiology Stem Cell Core (Core B) are: 1) To generate, perform QC, expand and maintain high-quality iPSC lines. 2) To perform CRISPR mutagenesis to generate isogenic lines with high-priority missense and nonsense mutations. 3) To generate human iPSC-derived excitatory/inhibitory neuron cocultures.

title: TrmD-targeting actinobacterial natural products as next generation antibiotics
text:
We have shown that targeting TrmD, a conserved and essential tRNA methyl transferase in bacteria, reduces
protein synthesis in general and biosynthesis of the Gram-negative double-membrane structure in particular,
suggesting a dual-strategy to accelerate bactericidal action. While many small molecular compound libraries
have been screened to target TrmD, isolated hits lack the cell-permeability necessary to exhibit an antibacterial
effect. We propose to screen a large collection of microbial extracts and fractions to target TrmD, using a novel
and HTS-ready Ec tolC+ cell-based assay, to identify NPs that are cell-permeable, resistant to efflux, and
selective of targeting, which will serve as leads for the next generation of antibiotics with a novel mechanism of
action distinct from those currently in clinical use.

title: Unraveling the Viral Infection Pathway with Virus-locked Observation
text:
Methods for evaluating the fate of single virions have led to a wealth of information on disease
states but have been primarily limited to surface studies and artificial culture environments. This
work will develop and apply high-speed 3D single-virus tracking methods to capture how viruses
such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2 navigate the complex epithelial space. Outcomes from this
work will shed light on the mechanisms through which virions traverse the first line of defense of
the human immune system.

title: Next-Generation Thalamic Nuclei Visualization and Segmentation Methods
text:
The thalamus and its subdivisions called nuclei play a critical role not only as a relay to the cerebral cortex but
also in memory, emotion, consciousness, and arousal and have been implicated in many neurological and
psychiatric disorders. Thalamic nuclei are not easily visualized in conventional MRI and specialized methods
proposed for visualization and segmentation of thalamic nuclei are still not accurate, especially for small nuclei.
The novel methods for improved visualization and automated segmentation of thalamic nuclei developed in this
grant will help identify biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity to be used in future studies for the
identification, evaluation, and monitoring of treatment strategies in different conditions like Alzheimer’s disease,
schizophrenia, and essential tremor.

title: Mapping transient interactions with and on genomic DNA
text:
Transcription occurs on genomic DNA throughout the cell cycle, including during the S-phase when DNA is
replicated: collisions between replication and transcription complexes have the potential to lead to DNA damage
and genome instability. One project will map and characterize direct physical interactions between transcribing
RNA polymerases and components of the replication machinery, allowing us to understand where these conflicts
occur and how their impact on genome integrity is mitigated. A second, related project takes advantage of a new
method we have recently developed to identify where DNA helicases – proteins that unwind DNA – are acting in
cells: we will apply this method to study how partially redundant helicases compensate for one another when
one is absent, and how their activities are regulated through the cell cycle.

title: Ferroptosis and Cancer Cell Signaling
text:
Success of the proposed research will unveil in-depth mechanisms of ferroptosis, as well as its functional
communication with various cancer-relevant intercellular and intracellular molecular events. The proposed
research will also lead to the identification of biomarkers that predict cancer responsiveness to future ferroptosis-
inducing cancer therapy.

title: Neuroimaging-guided Immunotherapy for Glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastomas are complex and deadly brain tumors with no current effective, long-term treatments.
This NIH COBRE project aims to develop a novel multimodal imaging platform to better understand two
promising antiangiogenic therapies to treat glioblastoma by in vivo longitudinal tracking of migrating
tumor cells, infiltrating immune cells, and tumor microvascular dynamics. Combined with spatial
transcriptomics, a machine learning based platform will be developed to guide and optimize the
treatment delivery in future human clinical studies.

title: Stress reactivity and adverse placental and pregnancy outcomes
text: Measuring stress reactivity in addition to stress exposure will help provide important insights into the mechanisms underlying adverse pregnancy outcomes. Given the growing evidence that APOs serve as an early warning sign for future CVD risk, our findings have important implications for cardiovascular disease risk as well.

title: Understanding Frontotemporal Dementia Using Drosophila and iPSC Models
text:
Frontotemporal lobal degeneration (FTLD) is a leading cause of dementia and the underlying molecular
pathogenic mechanisms are largely unknown. Multidisciplinary approaches—including molecular, cellular and
genetic analyses in fruitfly Drosophila and patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived
cortical neurons—will be used to identify and investigate novel molecular pathways that can modulate disease
phenotypes. If successful, these studies will identify new molecular targets and pathways for therapeutic
development for frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and related neurodegenerative disorders.

title: AI-Powered Quantitative Systems Pharmacology for AD Drug Repurposing
text:
Relevance Statement
Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a triple threat – with soaring prevalence, enormous costs and lack
of effective treatment. However, AD is a complex disease that has been extremely hard to treat
with the conventional approach. New methods that can reuse old drugs to target mulple
pathological processes in AD may provide new solutions to effective AD treatment.

title: Functional significance of plasma cell infiltrates of human cardiac allograft vasculopathy
text:
Multiple lines of evidence support an important role for local antibody responses in the pathophysiology of cardiac
allograft vasculopathy. To date, however, the specificity and function of intragraft plasma cells in human CAV
remain unclear. Our studies will use patient specimens to characterize these cells and understand how they
contribute to the rejection process.

title: Deep-learning assisted photoacoustic histology for real-time intraoperative pathological diagnosis
text:
The rapid histopathological examination can allow for an accurate intraoperative diagnosis and confirm negative
tumor margins in the resected tissue (i.e., suggesting all of the cancer has been removed), providing surgical
guidance and avoiding second surgeries. Currently, the intraoperative diagnosis in clinical practices relies mostly
on the frozen section technique, which usually suffers from compromised diagnostic interpretation due to
processing artifacts and only applies to limited tissue types. To address these challenges, I propose developing
the deep learning-assisted photoacoustic histology platform to generate readily interpretable computer-aided
images for pathologists and surgeons to diagnose intraoperatively and remotely.

title: Drug repurposing of a novel synthetic progestin for the prevention of preterm labor and fetal inflammation
text:
Intrauterine inflammation is an important cause of preterm labor and injury to the brain, lung
and GI tract of the unborn fetus and thus constitutes a major public health problem in this population. This grant
will study the efficacy of R5020 in preventing preterm labor and intrauterine inflammation in Rhesus macaques.
This knowledge will be important to develop treatment approaches aimed at improving maternal and child health.

title: Control of lung alveolar regeneration by Dot1L/H3K79 methylation
text:
Repair and regeneration of the lung alveoli are essential to restore the ability of gas exchange after lung injury.
The molecular pathways that drive this process are poorly understood. The current proposal seeks to
characterize a newly identified epigenetic and potentially druggable process that regulates how cells differentiate
and reprogram from one state to another.

title: SCH: Fair and Interpretable Prediction of Alzheimer's Disease and MCI using LLMs
text: Language alterations are informative markers of the AD trajectory, and these alterations may be detectable using large language models (LLMs). We will address the critical public health challenge of early detection of AD and MCI by investigating the fair and responsible use of LLMs for this purpose. This project will advance the understanding of language changes in early AD and lay groundwork for fair access to cognitive health assessment, potentially alleviating burden on the healthcare system.

title: Impact of Bariatric Surgery on the Risk of Adverse Oral Health Outcomes
text:
This retrospective study proposes to combine registry data of subjects who have undergone metabolic and
bariatric surgery (Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, sleeve gastrectomy, gastric banding, and biliopancreatic
diversion) with the Utah Population Database, to determine the oral health outcomes of bariatric surgery, with
specific reference to oral health complications and associated healthcare cost. Findings will provide important
oral health insights for patients with severe obesity and their healthcare providers, along with specific clinical
guidance on the relationship between metabolic and bariatric surgery and potential oral health implications.

title: Improving inclusion of individuals with intellectual disability in autism neuroscience research
text: Despite representing a substantial portion of autistic people, individuals with autism and intellectual disability are not usually studied in neuroscience research, and little is known about brain differences in this group. This project addresses this knowledge gap by investigating measures of social and communicative behavior and brain activity in this important segment of the autism spectrum. This research introduces innovative methods to reduce barriers and advance clinical research by understanding more about autism and intellectual disability.

title: The Role of Gm4951 in Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
text:
The rising prevalence of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has become a major public health concern.
Our proposed studies aim to understand the molecular mechanism of a new form of NAFLD identified from
mouse forward genetic screen. This research will have the potential to reveal novel therapeutic targets to reduce
NAFLD.

title: Cannabis effects on physical and mental health in medical cannabis patients
text:
With the rapid increase in medicinal cannabis use, there is an urgent need to identify patients who are at-risk
for cannabis use disorder, which can occur as an unintended adverse effect of using medicinal cannabis.
Importantly, not all patients who use medicinal cannabis develop addiction or a pathological pattern of
cannabis use (cannabis use disorder). This longitudinal study will collect new data on cannabis use in relation
to health at micro (daily) and macro (follow-up over 2-years) time scales to understand the roles of tolerance
and withdrawal (symptoms often experienced when taking medication as recommended) in likelihood of
addiction among medicinal cannabis patients, and will identify risk factors for cannabis use disorder as a
possible iatrogenic effect of using medicinal cannabis to inform clinical practice guidelines.
